record.paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
record.original_question: In a heterogeneous computing environment, how should the uncertainty in estimated parameter values, such as predicted task completion times, be incorporated into the process of mapping tasks and subtasks to machines?

evidence.quote: Distributed high-performance heterogeneous computing (HC) environments are composed of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed links.
Also, the uncertainty present in the estimated parameter values, such as task completion times, should be taken into consideration in determining the mappings.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous computing environment consisting of a finite set of machines $M = \{m_1, \ldots, m_p\}$ with varied computational capabilities interconnected by communication links, and a finite set of tasks (or subtasks) $T = \{t_1, \ldots, t_n\}$, possibly with precedence constraints given by a directed acyclic graph. For each pair $(t_i, m_j)$, the execution time, communication cost, and any other relevant parameters (e.g., energy consumption, machine availability, link bandwidth) are not known exactly but are estimated. Model these estimates as random variables $X_{ij}$ on a probability space, with known distributions (or at least known means, variances, or confidence intervals).

A mapping is a function $\mu : T \to M$ (together, when applicable, with a schedule assigning start times) and the performance of $\mu$ is measured by an objective such as the makespan
$$C_{\max}(\mu) = \max_{t_i \in T} C_i(\mu),$$
where $C_i(\mu)$ is the (random) completion time of task $t_i$ under $\mu$.

Develop a principled framework for incorporating the uncertainty in the estimated parameters into the mapping process. Specifically:

1. Define a precise notion of an "uncertainty-aware" optimal mapping (e.g., minimizing $\mathbb{E}[C_{\max}(\mu)]$, minimizing a quantile $\inf\{c : \Pr[C_{\max}(\mu) \le c] \ge 1-\alpha\}$, or minimizing a robust worst-case objective $\sup_{X \in \mathcal{U}} C_{\max}(\mu; X)$ over an uncertainty set $\mathcal{U}$).
2. Provide algorithms that produce such mappings, together with provable approximation or robustness guarantees relative to the chosen objective.
3. Quantify how the quality of the resulting mapping degrades as a function of the uncertainty (e.g., the variance or radius of $\mathcal{U}$) in the input estimates.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of incorporating parameter uncertainty into task-to-machine mapping in heterogeneous computing remains an active research area. Numerous approaches (stochastic, robust, and probabilistic robust mapping; static and dynamic heuristics; recent learning-based schedulers) have been proposed since the question was raised, but no single accepted framework or optimal solution exists, and the underlying stochastic scheduling problems are generally NP-hard with only partial approximation results known.

status_evidence.title: Robust static allocation of resources for independent tasks under makespan and dollar cost constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Studies robust resource allocation in heterogeneous computing under uncertain task execution times.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on uncertainty-aware mapping in HC environments.

status_evidence.title: Stochastic scheduling on unrelated machines
status_evidence.snippet: Approximation algorithms for stochastic scheduling problems with random processing times.
status_evidence.claim: The general stochastic mapping problem is NP-hard with only approximation results known.
